inspection_summary: Inspected all 675 logical lines of the hash-bound normalized preprint, including 661 LF-delimited records and 14 form-feed page boundaries. Its strongest reusable mechanism is to treat a completed zeta or L-function as the Fourier symbol of a pseudodifferential operator and then use an assumed regularized Hadamard factorization to decompose the nonlocal quadratic form into local Klein-Gordon-like factors indexed by zeros. The article itself repeatedly marks important steps as formal, assumed, conjectural, or requiring further investigation; the cosmological and Langlands applications are proposals rather than established consequences. Prose is readable, but several central product, field-redefinition, gamma-factor, and exponent displays have damaged alignment or glyphs, so exact formula use requires verification against the retained PDF.

accepted_units.title: Replace an undefined prime-wise operator product by an analytic zeta symbol
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction begins with prime-indexed kinetic operators, observes that their naive adelic product lacks an evident mathematical meaning, and uses the Euler product as motivation for a single pseudodifferential symbol built from zeta. This is a clear bridge-construction move from an unusable factor-level expression to a globally defined analytic object.
accepted_units.context_note: The proposed shift by one half and the interpretation of zeros as a spectrum are motivated by the Riemann hypothesis; lines 72-75 correctly present the later equivalence as conditional rather than evidence for the hypothesis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on distinguishing a formal product over primes, the Euler product in its valid domain, and substitution of the d'Alembertian into an analytic symbol. The displayed one-half shift is vertically split; verify equations (1)-(3) against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Completion turns zeta into an entire critical-line-real function encoded by its nontrivial zeros
accepted_units.why_material: The section moves from the Dirichlet/Euler representations to the theta-Mellin completion xi, whose entire continuation, functional equation, critical-line reality, zero symmetries, and Hadamard product make it a more suitable operator symbol. The product representation exposes zeros as factor data for the subsequent field decomposition.
accepted_units.context_note: This is collected background rather than a new proof in the article. The zero-counting asymptotic and RH statement provide context, while the reusable mechanism is the completion-plus-factorization representation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires exact gamma and pi normalization, theta functional equation, conjugation/reflection symmetries, and regularized Hadamard product. Several fractions and product indices are layout-degraded; check equations (4)-(16) against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Define an analytic function of the wave operator through multiplication in Fourier space
accepted_units.why_material: The source gives an explicit operational meaning to F(box): Fourier transform the field, multiply by F(k squared), and invert. It then chooses xi on the critical line because boundedness gives a stated convergence condition and records the distinction between this symbol substitution and later quantization of the field.
accepted_units.context_note: The definition is made only in Minkowski space and under a convergence assumption on the Fourier integral. It does not by itself supply a general operator-domain or curved-space theory.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Fourier conventions, Lorentzian sign choices, and the complex argument of xi. Equations (17)-(21), especially the integral representation of the quantized xi symbol, require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: A regularized Hadamard product decomposes a nonlocal quadratic form into zero-indexed local factors
accepted_units.why_material: The central proposition rewrites the xi symbol as paired linear factors associated with critical-line zeros and introduces projected fields so that the original nonlocal quadratic Lagrangian becomes a sum of Klein-Gordon-like terms. It is the article's main example of converting analytic zero data into local mode data.
accepted_units.context_note: The derivation assumes critical-line zeros, a regularization of the infinite product, and sufficient simplicity to use coefficients involving the derivative at each zero. The article calls the final equivalence straightforward and does not supply convergence or functional-analytic details.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong formula dependency: the regularized product, normalization constant, projected-field product excluding one factor, and eta coefficient are central. Equation (30) is visibly garbled in normalized text; equations (22)-(31) must be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Curvature breaks the flat Fourier definition, motivating a factorized local surrogate
accepted_units.why_material: The authors explicitly identify that xi of the curved d'Alembertian lacks the straightforward Fourier definition available in Minkowski space. They propose using a regularized Hadamard product to replace it by a sum of local zero-indexed fields, thereby separating a genuine definition problem from a formal workaround.
accepted_units.context_note: The claimed equivalence in curved spacetime is asserted by analogy with the previous proposition, not proved in the displayed text. Subsequent cosmological solutions therefore inherit this unresolved foundation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on a choice of functional calculus for the curved d'Alembertian, regularization of the infinite product, and covariance of the decomposition. Exact equations (36)-(37) need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Factorized classical modes suggest a spectral two-point function, but its mathematical meaning remains open
accepted_units.why_material: The article promotes the field to an operator-valued distribution, requires its Wightman function to satisfy the nonlocal equation, and writes a formal Kallen-Lehmann-like sum supported on the zero-derived mass shells. It then explicitly states that the expression needs further mathematical investigation and notes the resulting ghost/tachyon possibilities.
accepted_units.context_note: This is not a constructed quantum field theory: existence of the state space, vacuum, positivity, Lorentz invariance, and spectral distribution are assumed or potentially violated.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires distribution theory, mass-shell delta functions, indefinite metric, and the regularized mode decomposition. The sum/integral layout is incomplete, so exact spectral weights must be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A phase-corrected zeta transform supplies another real symbol with the same critical-line zeros
accepted_units.why_material: The Riemann-Siegel function removes the critical-line phase so that a real function of a real variable carries the relevant zeros. The section compares zero locations with Gram points, records their shared n/log n scale, and proposes using this bounded real transform as an alternative operator symbol.
accepted_units.context_note: Gram's law is explicitly described as empirical tendency, not a theorem without exceptions. The resulting field theory is only proposed, not analyzed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the exact gamma-phase normalization, Gram-point convention, Lambert-W approximation, and asymptotic comparison. Equations (43)-(47) are formula-sensitive and need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Changing the L-function character changes zero symmetries and therefore the proposed mode pairing
accepted_units.why_material: For primitive Dirichlet characters the completed L-function again has an entire-product representation, but non-real characters need not have zeros symmetric about the real axis. The authors use this contrast to suggest that symbol choice can alter the paired spectrum and its ghost/tachyon interpretation.
accepted_units.context_note: The analytic continuation and product structure are background facts; the claim that a suitable character avoids pathological modes is speculative and is not demonstrated by an example or spectral analysis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires the completed Dirichlet L normalization, conjugation properties of characters, and a justified map from complex zero geometry to real field modes. Verify equation (48) and the proposed operator argument against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A Mellin-transformed Dirichlet series certifies modular origin through continuation and functional equation
accepted_units.why_material: The passage states the elliptic-curve/modular-form bridge in analytic terms: Fourier coefficients define a Dirichlet L-series, and holomorphic continuation plus a functional equation characterize its modular role. It situates L-functions as representation-independent carriers of arithmetic structure before operator substitution.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a compact historical/background statement of the modularity theorem and its implication for Fermat's Last Theorem, not a proof or a developed quantization mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the exact weight-two normalization and Mellin-transform functional equation, neither of which is displayed in full. The extracted Fourier exponent may be missing the imaginary unit; verify against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: An arithmetic vanishing order becomes the leading multiplicity of the substituted operator
accepted_units.why_material: The article pairs the Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer statement that the order of vanishing at one equals the elliptic-curve rank with the formal expansion of L(1+i box), in which the same order becomes the leading power of the differential operator. This is a concise example of translating analytic multiplicity into operator multiplicity.
accepted_units.context_note: BSD is presented as a conjecture, and the article does not justify the operator expansion, its coefficient, domain, or physical interpretation. The unit preserves the proposed structural translation only.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires analyticity near s=1, the exact leading coefficient, and a valid functional calculus for L(1+i box). The ellipsis hides all higher terms, so no dynamical conclusion is supported.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Entire-function factorization can localize a nonlocal symbol only after domain and regularization choices are fixed
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Completion supplies an entire symbol with a zero product, Fourier functional calculus turns that symbol into a nonlocal operator, and formal partial-factor projections convert the quadratic form into zero-indexed local modes.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source assumes regularization, critical-line/simple-zero structure, convergence, and suitable field domains; it does not establish an unconditional Hilbert-space equivalence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Reality and reflection symmetry of the chosen completion determine whether zero-derived modes can be paired
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Xi and the phase-corrected Riemann-Siegel transform are real on the critical line and support conjugate pairing, whereas completed L-functions of non-real characters can lose real-axis symmetry and thereby alter the proposed factor pairing.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The physical ghost/tachyon conclusion is conjectural; zero symmetry alone does not establish positivity, stability, or a viable quantum theory.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A representation change does not remove the obligation to define the operator on the new geometry
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Flat Fourier multiplication gives a concrete starting definition, but curved spacetime removes that diagonal representation and quantum-field promotion adds distributional and positivity requirements. Factorized mode formulas are proposals for handling these changes, not automatic extensions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The article supplies neither a curved spectral calculus nor a constructed Wightman theory, so the synthesis identifies an obligation and proposed route rather than a solved problem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic multiplicities can carry arithmetic information into an operator expansion without validating the physical interpretation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Modularity packages arithmetic data into an analytically continued L-function, while a zero of order r at a distinguished point formally becomes a leading operator power of order r after symbol substitution.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The relevant arithmetic statements include conjectural cases, and the formal operator series does not by itself yield observable states, masses, or cosmological constants.

within_source_saturation: Saturated for distinct source-supported conceptual mechanisms. The plan retains the adelic reframing, completion and zero factorization, flat functional calculus, formal localization, curved and quantum definition gaps, alternative real symbol, zero-symmetry comparison, modular L-function bridge, and vanishing-order translation. Remaining mathematical prose is standard background without a new developed move, elementary downstream mode algebra, or broad physical/number-theoretic speculation explicitly left unproved or for future work.
stop_reason: All 675 logical lines were inspected. Further units would elevate routine cosmological calculations, bibliographic summaries of major conjectures, or unsupported claims about singularities, the cosmological constant, Langlands, motives, and random matrices. The one central extraction-corrupt field redefinition is quarantined at line level and every formula-dependent accepted unit records its PDF-verification boundary.
